questions_and_answers.question_text: What is gōngshāngyè a compound of?
What kind of verb is fādá, and what must you not confuse it with?
How does a question word come to mean "every" or "any"?
What do you agree with in Chinese — a person or an idea?
What form does NOT exist in Chinese?
Write the Chinese for "I agree with him (his ideas)."
Write the Chinese for "This country is very prosperous."
Which verb can take an object — fādá or fāzhǎn?

answers.answer_text: Fāzhǎn, the action verb — e.g., fāzhǎn nóngyè, "to develop agriculture."

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "He doesn't approve of their getting married."
What does tóngyì mean as a noun?

articles.text:
6. A: Gōngshāngyè fādá yǒu shénme    What benefit is there in having a
      hǎochu? Nǎli dōu nàme zāng!    flourishing industry and commerce?
                                      It's so dirty everywhere!
   B: Zhèi yìdiǎn wǒ bù tóngyì,      I don't agree with that. There are a
      gōngshāngyè fādá yǒu bù shǎo   lot of benefits to having a flourishing
      hǎochu.                        industry and commerce.

Notes on No. 6

gōngshāngyè: "industry and commerce." This is a compound of gōngyè, "industry," and shāngyè, "commerce." Gōngyè and nóngyè can also combine as gōngnóngyè.

fādá: "to be developed, to be well-developed; to be prosperous, to be flourishing." This is an ADJECTIVAL VERB — it describes a STATE or condition. In addition to describing industry, fādá can describe a person's muscular build or a developed country.

Zhèige guójiā hěn fādá.          This country is very prosperous.
Tāmen nàrde wénhuà hěn fādá.     The culture there is very developed.

Do NOT confuse the STATE verb fādá with the ACTION verb fāzhǎn, which CAN take an object, e.g., fāzhǎn nóngyè, "to develop agriculture."

nǎli dōu...: "everywhere." Here you see another example of a QUESTION WORD used to mean "every..." or "any...". You must use nǎli (or shéi, shénme) BEFORE dōu or yě.

Tā shénme dìfang dōu bú qù.      He is not going anywhere.
Shéi dōu qù.                     Everybody is going.
Zěnme zuò dōu bù xíng.           Any way you do it, it just doesn't work.

tóngyì: "to agree, to consent; agreement, consent." As a verb, the meaning is the same as in English. BUT there is a DIFFERENCE in how you say WHO it is you agree with. In Chinese, you don't agree WITH A PERSON; you agree with an IDEA, opinion, statement.

Tāde xiǎngfǎ nǐ tóngyì ma?       Do you agree with his opinion?
Wǒ tóngyì tāde kànfǎ.            I agree with him (his ideas).

CAUTION: Speakers of English often want to say gēn...tóngyì because we say "agree WITH..." in English, but THERE IS NO SUCH FORM IN CHINESE.

Tóngyì may also be directly followed by a clause:

Tā bù tóngyì tāmen jiéhūn.       He doesn't approve of their getting
                                 married.

As a NOUN, tóngyì means "agreement" or "consent."
